attacks.claim: Family Code article 68 makes custody forfeit when the person entitled does not claim it for more than one year without excuse, so the custody request has a time limit. The record cites articles 62, 64, 65 and 66 but not 68, has no deadline on custody, and no slot asks when the children left the wife's care.

source.what: Law 84-11 of 9 June 1984 (Family Code), article 68, Official Journal 1984 issue 24, page 914 (PDF page 6), right-hand column. The article store lists article 68 as version law-84-11, never amended.

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 68 : اذا لم يطلب من له الحق فى الحضانة مدة تزيد عن سنة بدون عذر سقط حقه فيها.
attacks.consequence: A common case: the wife left the marital home 14 months before filing, the children stayed with the husband or his mother, and she never claimed custody. The record drafts r3 (custody to the plaintiff) and gives no warning. It should carry a custody time item based on article 68: ask the date the children left her care and whether she had an excuse, and warn past one year. How the year is counted and the meaning of «عذر» are open readings.

attacks.claim: A wife whose husband is missing is not covered. If a court has already declared him dead under Law 03-06 (persons missing after the earthquake of 21 May 2003) or Ordinance 06-01 (missing persons of the national tragedy), the marriage is already dissolved by death (Family Code article 47), and the declaration has 'all the legal effects'. If he is missing but not yet declared dead, Family Code article 112 sends his wife to a divorce request under article 53, item 5 (absence), not to khul against a defendant who cannot attend the mandatory reconciliation hearing. The record's only 'marriage already dissolved' boundary, n1, fires on spouses_divorced, a prior divorce judgment. Nothing asks about a death declaration or a missing husband.

source.what: Law 03-06 of 14 June 2003, articles 2 and 3, Official Journal 2003 issue 37, page 9. Ordinance 06-01 of 27 February 2006 (Charter for Peace and National Reconciliation), articles 28, 29, 30 and 36, Official Journal 2006 issue 11, page 6. Family Code articles 47, 59 and 112 (article store, version law-84-11).

attacks.quoteArabic: قانون 03-06، المادة 3: «يخول الحكم القاضي بوفاة المفقود المذكور في المادة 2 أعلاه، الحق في كل الآثار القانونية المنصوص عليها في التشريع المعمول به.» ؛ الأمر 06-01، المادة 29: «بغض النظر عن الأحكام المنصوص عليها في قانون الأسرة، تطبق الأحكام الواردة في هذا القسم على المفقودين المذكورين في المادة 28 أعلاه.» والمادة 36 فقرة 2: «وتترتب عليه مجموع الآثار القانونية المنصوص عليها في التشريع المعمول به.» ؛ قانون الأسرة المادة 112: «لزوجة المفقود أو الغائب أن تطلب الطلاق بناء على الفقرة الخامسة من المادة 53 من هذا القانون.»
attacks.consequence: Case: the husband disappeared years ago and a judgment declared him dead, or a judgment found him missing. The wife asks for khul to be free to remarry. The record drafts r1 (khul for a consideration offered to a husband who is dead or missing), and n1 stays silent. The record should ask whether the husband is missing or has been declared dead. When he is declared dead, it should warn that the marriage is dissolved by death (article 47). When he is missing, it should warn that the route is article 112 with article 53 item 5 (tatliq), and that article 59 sets the waiting period from the judgment of disappearance.

attacks.claim: The record states the reconciliation step (Family Code 49, CPCA 439 to 443) but leaves out the arbitration step. Family Code article 56 says that when the dispute between the spouses intensifies and no harm is proved, two arbiters 'must' be appointed, one from each family, to report within two months. CPCA 446 lets the judge appoint them when no harm is proved, and CPCA 447 to 449 organise their work. A khul claim is by definition one where the wife proves no harm, so it is the typical case for these texts.

source.what: Family Code article 56 (law 84-11, unchanged per the store), Official Journal 1984 issue 24, page 913. CPCA (law 08-09) articles 446 to 449, Official Journal 2008 issue 21, page 38.

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 56 : اذا اشتد الخصام بين الزوجين ولم يثبت الضرر وجب تعيين حكمين للتوفيق بينهما. يعين القاضي الحكمين، حكما من أهل الزوج وحكما من أهل الزوجة، وعلى هذين الحكمين أن يقدما تقريرا عن مهمتهما فى أجل شهرين. ؛ المادة 446 (ق.إ.م.إ): إذا لم يثبت أي ضرر أثناء الخصومة، جاز للقاضي أن يعين حكمين اثنين لمحاولة الصلح بينهما حسب مقتضيات قانون الأسرة.
attacks.consequence: k46 says no sanction for an omitted attempt is stated, and k8 and k45 describe only the three-month reconciliation window. The record should cite FC 56 and CPCA 446 to 449, and note that an arbiters' mission (two months) may follow the reconciliation and lengthen the case. Whether FC 56 «وجب» or CPCA 446 «جاز» governs a khul claim is a reading to record as an open point. The record must not imply that reconciliation is the only step before the merits.

attacks.claim: The record states the waiting period only for a wife who is not pregnant (b23: three cycles or three months). Family Code article 60, which the record does not cite, makes a pregnant wife's waiting period last until delivery, up to ten months from the divorce. So for a wife pregnant at the khul, the waiting-period maintenance r2 asks for, and her right to stay in the home under article 61, cover a different period from the one the record states.

source.what: Family Code article 60 (law 84-11, unchanged per the store), Official Journal 1984 issue 24, page 913.

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 60 : عدة الحامل وضع حملها، وأقصى مدة الحمل عشرة (10) أشهر من تاريخ الطلاق أو الوفاة.
attacks.consequence: Case: the wife is four months pregnant when she files for khul. k24 tells the lawyer the waiting period is three cycles or three months, so the amount asked as waiting-period maintenance is understated. The record should cite article 60, ask whether the wife is pregnant, and adjust the waiting-period text and the r2 wording. The child's future maintenance and lineage questions also arise.

attacks.claim: The territorial rule t1 rests only on CPCA article 40 ¶3. It ignores CPCA article 426, the family section's own territorial rule. Article 426 adds three courts the record does not give: visitation goes to the place custody is exercised (item 4), household goods (the restitution request r5) go to the marital home (item 6), and disputes over the dowry go to the defendant's domicile (item 8). So t1 is silent on r5 and r7, and wrong-footed for any unpaid deferred dowry that k20 invites the lawyer to raise.

source.what: Law 08-09 of 25 February 2008 (CPCA), article 426, Official Journal 2008 issue 21, page 36, left column. Not touched by Law 22-13 per the ledger.

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 426 : تكون المحكمة مختصة إقليميا : ... 3 - في موضوع الطلاق أو الرجوع بمكان وجود المسكن الزوجي ... 4 - في موضوع الحضانة وحق الزيارة والرخص الإدارية المسلمة للقاصر المحضون بمكان ممارسة الحضانة، 5 - في موضوع النفقة الغذائية بموطن الدائن بها، 6 - في موضوع متاع بيت الزوجية بمكان وجود المسكن الزوجي، ... 8 - في موضوع المنازعة حول الصداق بمكان موطن المدعى عليه،
attacks.consequence: t1 should cite CPCA 426 next to article 40. It should give the restitution of household goods to the marital-home court (which agrees with the khul court) and visitation to the place of custody. When a dowry claim is joined, it should warn that article 426 item 8 points to the defendant's domicile. o9 should list these items too.

attacks.claim: Item b32 and checklist line k17 say custody 'ends' at ten for a boy and at marriage age for a girl. Article 65 ¶2, which is not cited, makes the judgment ending custody subject to the child's interest. The record cites ¶1 alone and presents the ages as automatic.

source.what: Family Code article 65 ¶2 (law 84-11, unchanged per the store), Official Journal 1984 issue 24, page 914.

attacks.quoteArabic: على أن يراعى فى الحكم بانتهائها مصلحة المحضون.
attacks.consequence: Case: a boy is 10 years and 3 months old and the wife asks for his custody with the khul. Read from b32, the record suggests the request is out of time, but the text leaves the end of custody to the judge, weighed against the child's interest. b32 should cite ¶2, and k17 should not present the ages as automatic. The same goes for article 67 ¶2 to ¶3 (the mother's work is no ground for losing custody), which bear on e4's fitness element.

attacks.claim: Law 15-01 created the alimony fund (صندوق النفقة). The fund pays the maintenance a court has awarded to custodial children, including maintenance awarded provisionally while a divorce claim is pending, and the maintenance awarded to the divorced woman, when the debtor does not pay or cannot be found. The application goes to the president of the family section. The record's maintenance and provisional-measure requests never mention it. Asking for a provisional maintenance order in the khul claim is what opens this route.

source.what: Law 15-01 of 4 January 2015 creating the alimony fund, articles 2 to 6, Official Journal 2015 issue 1, pages 7 and 8. No amendment was searched for beyond this issue.

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 2 : ... النفقة: النفقة المحكوم بها وفقا لأحكام قانون الأسرة لصالح الطفل أو الأطفال المحضونين بعد طلاق الوالدين، وكذلك النفقة المحكوم بها مؤقتا لصالح الطفل أو الأطفال في حالة رفع دعوى الطلاق والنفقة المحكوم بها للمرأة المطلقة، ... المادة 3 : يتم دفع المستحقات المالية للمستفيد، إذا تعذر التنفيذ الكلي أو الجزئي للأمر أو الحكم القضائي المحدد لمبلغ النفقة، بسبب امتناع المدين بها عن الدفع أو عجزه عن ذلك أو لعدم معرفة محل إقامته.
attacks.consequence: This changes no rule of the petition. r6 and k21 should note that a provisional maintenance order for the children, made during the khul claim, is itself a title the fund can pay on (law 15-01 art. 2). This matters most when the husband lives abroad or cannot be found (n8, k64).

attacks.claim: The record says the former wording of article 54 is not available and keeps from memory that 'the courts required the husband's consent' before 2005 (k3, o7, grade D). The 1984 wording is on the Official Journal page. It already let the judge fix the consideration when the spouses do not agree, and its text names no condition of the husband's consent. Whether the courts required consent was contested in the Supreme Court's own decisions, so k3 states as settled history what was not. Ordinance 05-02 replaced the article. Former article 57 also lacked the present ¶2 on custody appeals.

source.what: Family Code (law 84-11) original articles 54 and 57, Official Journal 1984 issue 24, page 913. Tier-3 lead for the case-law point: an academic study (Univ. M'sila, num.univ-msila.dz, 2024) citing Supreme Court decisions 31729, 33632 and 36731 published in المجلة القضائية as inconsistent on consent. These decisions were not read on the Court's site.

attacks.quoteArabic: المادة 54 : يجوز للزوجة أن تخالع نفسها من زوجها على مال يتم الاتفاق عليه فان لم يتفقا على شيء يحكم القاضي بما لا يتجاوز قيمة صداق المثل وقت الحكم. ؛ المادة 57 : الاحكام بالطلاق غير قابلة للاستئناف ما عدا فى جوانبها المادية.
attacks.consequence: o7 should hold the former wording with its source and drop the claim that it 'turned on agreement on the consideration' as the only reading. k3 should not tell the lawyer that consent was required before 2005 as a fact. For facts and judgments before the ordinance, the former article 57 has no custody-appeal paragraph.
